{"text": "import opentrons
from opentrons import protocol_api

metadata = {"protocolName": "PCR setup for 8 samples", "apiLevel": "2.19"}

def run(protocol: protocol_api.ProtocolContext):
    # Load labware
    tube_rack = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_24_tuberack_nest_1.5ml_snapcap", 1)
    plate = protocol.load_labware("nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt", 2)
    tiprack = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_96_tiprack_20ul", 3)
    
    # Pipette
    p20 = protocol.load_instrument("p20_single_gen2", "right", tip_racks=[tiprack])
    
    # Define liquids
    master_mix = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="master mix",
        description="PCR master mix",
        display_color="#FF0000"
    )
    sample_liquids = {}
    for i in range(1, 9):
        liq = protocol.define_liquid(
            name=f"sample {i}",
            description=f"DNA sample {i}",
            display_color="#00FF00"
        )
        sample_liquids[f"sample {i}"] = liq
    
    # Load liquids into wells (starting volumes)
    tube_rack["A1"].load_liquid(master_mix, volume=500)  # master mix
    for i in range(1, 9):
        well_name = chr(ord('A') + i) + "1"  # B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1, H1
        tube_rack[well_name].load_liquid(sample_liquids[f"sample {i}"], volume=200)
    
    # Prepare reactions: wells A1-A8 in plate
    dest_wells = [f"A{i+1}" for i in range(8)]  # A1..A8
    
    for idx, well in enumerate(dest_wells, start=1):
        p20.pick_up_tip()
        # Add master mix (20 ul)
        p20.aspirate(20, tube_rack["A1"])
        p20.dispense(20, plate[well])
        # Add sample (5 ul)
        sample_well = tube_rack[f"{chr(ord('A')+idx)}1"]
        p20.aspirate(5, sample_well)
        p20.dispense(5, plate[well])
        p20.drop_tip()
"}

    plate = protocol.load_labware("nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt", 2)

    # Define liquids
    master_mix = protocol.define_liquid(

        description="PCR master mix",
        display_color="#FF0000"
    )
    sample_liquids = {}
    for i in range(1, 9):
        liq = protocol.define_liquid(
            name=f"sample {i}",
            description=f"DNA sample {i}",
            display_color="#00FF00"
        )
        sample_liquids[f"sample {i}"] = liq
    
    # Load liquids into wells (starting volumes)
    tube_rack["A1"].load_liquid(master_mix, volume=500)  # master mix
    sample_well_positions = ["B1", "C1", "D1", "A2", "B2", "C2", "D2", "A3"]
    for idx, pos in enumerate(sample_well_positions, start=1):
        tube_rack[pos].load_liquid(sample_liquids[f"sample {idx}"], volume=200)
    
    # Prepare reactions: wells A1-A8 in plate
    dest_wells = [f"A{i+1}" for i in range(8)]  # A1..A8
    
    for idx, well in enumerate(dest_wells, start=1):
        # Add master mix with fresh tip
        p20.pick_up_tip()
        p20.aspirate(20, tube_rack["A1"])
        p20.dispense(20, plate[well])
        p20.drop_tip()
        # Add sample with fresh tip and mix
        p20.pick_up_tip()
        sample_well = tube_rack[sample_well_positions[idx-1]]
        p20.aspirate(5, sample_well)
        p20.dispense(5, plate[well])
        p20.mix(5, 20, plate[well])  # mix 5 times 20ul
        p20.drop_tip()

protocol.py: 1 biology problem (1 note).

1. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 8 wells of master mix with a sample
   line 43:  p20.dispense(20, plate[well])
   At line 43 the robot starts putting master mix into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full
   Skirt (slot 2), and 8 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate
   holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is
   contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing
   on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and
   A8 in slot 2.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 2.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 20 ul of master mix and 5 ul of water in place of
   the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML

           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate

           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
